newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK PAVES WAY FOR CURRENCY BOARD.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK PAVES WAY FOR CURRENCY BOARD.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) paved the way on Thursday for a restrictive monetary regime aimed at boosting confidence in the crumbling financial system.
The BNB said in a statement it has decided to stop open market operations through daily reverse repo-auctions held so far to regulate commercial banks' short-term liquidity.
From January 20 the Finance Ministry will issue seven-day treasury bills to regulate excessive liquidity of banks.

"This decision is connected with preparing the banking system for the gradual implementation of the currency board under which open market operations will be curbed," Plamen Oresharski, head of the State Treasury and Debt department in the Finance Ministry, told Reuters.

In November the International Monetary Fund (IMF) proposed the introduction of the currency board system, which severely curbs the financial powers of the government and the central bank, to boost confidence in the crumbling financial structure.
Preparations for the currency board, due to be completed by February, include restructuring the central bank, passing in parliament a viable 1997 budget and approving amendments to banking laws.

The IMF had been expected to complete negotiations by end-January but a political crisis driven by massive street protests against mismanagement of the economy by the ruling Socialists and demands for early elections have postponed the agreement indefinitely.
The central bank asked parliament's budget and finance committee to approve stop-gap funding of the state budget until the 1997 budget is approved by parliament.
"After discussing the problems of domestic and foreign debt due...in the first quarter, the BNB board decided to ask parliament to adopt a stop-gap funding," said the statement.
Domestic and foreign debt due in January totals 180 billion levs. Expected budget revenue is estimated at 40 billion levs.

The step was aimed at guaranteeing the normal functioning of the budget until the introduction of a currency board, proposed by the International Monetary Fund as a last resort to halt the collapse of the national currency.
The government has to pay some 180 billion levs of its foreign and domestic debt in January. Expected budget revenue is estimated at 40 billion levs.
Bulgaria is expected to pay a $130 million coupon on Brady bonds issued two years ago to restructure a $8.1 billion commercial debt.
The BNB also plans to hike bank provision requirements in accordance with IMF and World Bank recommendations under new draft regulations, which were discussed on Thursday, said the statement.
